routeSelection.route: Ordinary full-time Chemistry bachelor; 36 EC all-BC1 example
routeSelection.basis: Ordinary current Chemistry route. Preserve prior permitted RNA and Magnetic Resonance selections; complete 36 EC with first six other distinct BC1 entries in adopted formal list order, independently of UCR fit. No formal specialisation or annual availability guarantee. Bounded prerequisite repair: replace Catalysis3 by its own preparatory Metal Organic Chemistry3; retain 36 EC and other sound choices. Advanced Molecular Biology is completed before RNA, using the second/third-year choice framework.

audience.programmeDescription: Students investigate how molecular structure determines properties and reactions. They combine synthetic, analytical, organic, inorganic and physical chemistry with mathematics, physics, laboratory training and an individual research internship.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR combination follows the chemistry of living systems from biomolecules and enzymes through molecular cell biology, genetics, laboratory methods and disease mechanisms. Radboud combines this strand with organic synthesis, physical and inorganic chemistry, quantum chemistry and specialist chemical laboratories.

curriculum.routeLabel: Ordinary full-time Chemistry bachelor; 36 EC Chemistry elective example
curriculum.limitation: The 180 EC comprises 126 EC of required courses, 36 EC of restricted scientific electives, a 12 EC individual research internship and 6 EC of free choice. All 36 EC in this example are selected Chemistry electives, rather than universally required courses; options may not run every year. Internship entry requires 120 EC including all first-year courses and prior proposal approval. First-year Academic Skills carries no extra credits; RADAr participation is required, but a passing score is not. The usual first-year study-advice threshold is 39 EC. Course entry, attendance, overlap and approval rules apply.

core: Molecular structure, biochemistry, cellular mechanisms and medicinal applications
Biomedical function, disease, pharmacology and molecular health research
Mathematics, programming, modelling and statistical analysis for scientific questions
Laboratory, field and independent scientific inquiry

questions: How do molecular and biochemical processes produce biological function, disease and treatment possibilities?
How can molecular and biomedical questions be investigated experimentally and quantitatively?
How can chemical and material processes support environmental remediation, circularity and sustainable resource use?

trace: Introduces empirical research design and statistical analysis, followed by a substantial student research project.
Introduces data analysis and visualization in R through practical work with tabular, textual and spatial data.
Introduces statistical learning for understanding data and predicting outcomes.
Examines how digital images are represented, processed and interpreted to recognize structures and objects.
Develops neural-network theory and practical implementation in Python, Keras and TensorFlow.
Introduces computational problem-solving and programming in Python.
Develops single-variable calculus and related mathematical tools for modelling scientific problems.
Provides a rigorous introduction to probability and mathematical statistics, from probability spaces and random variables to multivariate distributions and statistical inference.
Studies human anatomical structure in relation to function through regional and body-system blocks.
Studies how drugs act at molecular, cellular and whole-body levels and how the body handles them.
Examines host-microbe interactions and the immune mechanisms that protect against infection or cause disease.
Connects normal organ function to pathophysiology across digestive, cardiovascular, respiratory, renal, endocrine and nervous systems.
Studies nervous systems and behaviour from comparative, evolutionary and physiological perspectives.
Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action.
Deepens understanding of neuroanatomy, neurophysiology and the experimental study of higher cognitive functions.
Introduces the molecular and cellular foundations of life and biomedical science.
Introduces psychological and neuroscientific explanations of behaviour and mental processes.
Studies the molecular mechanisms underlying cellular structure, physiology and regulation, primarily in eukaryotes.
Studies normal function and regulation in the adult human body, linking molecular and cellular processes to integrated organ systems.
Examines the chemistry of life, emphasizing biomolecular structure and function, enzymes and metabolic pathways.
Provides hands-on training in biochemical, microbiological and molecular laboratory methods.
Connects cellular pathology with the genetic mechanisms of human disease.
Teaches systematic review and meta-analysis for synthesizing evidence in medical, behavioural and related research.
